roadmap.goal: Ship two controls for the metrics time window on Team and Portfolio dashboards: a row of named preset windows inside the existing date popover, and a back/forward stepper pair on the dashboard header that walks the same-length window through time. Source: ADO User Story #5914, tagged Release Notes, no parent Epic. Frontend only - no endpoint, DTO, EF migration, config key or client change (D14). The 66 acceptance tests are already authored by DISTILL and land skipped across four files; DELIVER implements production code and un-skips each describe block as it goes green. Two phases mirroring the two DISCUSS slices. The load-bearing work is in 01-02: the two existing per-end date setters each rebuild the URL from the other end's current-render value, so they cannot be composed to move a two-ended window - a single applyDateRange(start, end) write path replaces them and makes the torn write unreachable by construction.

out_of_scope: Changing the Team's opening range - TeamMetricsView.tsx:117-128 is not edited (D1)
Changing the Portfolio's opening range - PortfolioMetricsView.tsx:68 is not edited (D2)
Any persistence of the chosen window; it stays URL-only, no localStorage (D10)
Any RBAC gate or premium gate (D13)
Any backend change - no endpoint, DTO, EF migration or HistoricalSchemaPatch entry (D14)
Any Lighthouse-Clients CLI or MCP version bump (D15)
Constraining the manual end picker to today; it keeps no maxDate (D16)
Introducing dayjs onto the metrics date surface; date-fns only (D17)
Weakening useVisitedCategories' date-keyed reset token - Bug #5571's monotonic gate stands (DDD-9)
Changing DEBOUNCE_MS=300 for its existing callers; 500ms applies only to the metrics window (DDD-4)
Mutation testing, /nw-finalize, ADO transitions and pushing - the user reviews the delivered slices first
A previous-period overlay or per-widget delta; this feature moves the window, it does not draw two

phases.name: Named windows in one click
phases.description: Slice 01. A Delivery Lead opens the date popover on a Team's or Portfolio's metrics, clicks one named window, and the whole dashboard redraws over it with both ends of the window landing in the URL together. Introduces the combined two-ended setter that slice 02 is built on.

steps.name: dateWindow pure module - owner-aware presets, window algebra, forward clamp
criteria: getPresetsForOwner('team') returns exactly four presets in ascending order with labels 'Last 7 days', 'Last 14 days', 'Last 30 days', 'Last 90 days'; getPresetsForOwner('portfolio') returns exactly three with labels 'Last 30 days', 'Last 90 days', 'Last 180 days'
getStepDaysForOwner returns 7 for a team and 28 for a portfolio

presetWindow(days, today) returns end = today and start = today minus days, both as local calendar days; windowLengthInDays of that window equals days, including across a year boundary and across a daylight-saving transition
shiftWindow(window, stepDays) moves BOTH ends by stepDays and never changes windowLengthInDays; four successive -7 shifts land on exactly the same window as one -28 shift
canStepForward(window, today) is false when the window ends on today and false when it already ends after today; true only while the end is strictly before today

clampWindowToToday(window, today) moves a window whose end is after today back so the end lands exactly on today, moving the start by the same amount so the length is preserved; a window ending on or before today is returned unchanged

matchingPresetDays returns the preset's days only when the window both ends today AND has that preset's length; a hand-picked length returns null, and a window walked into the past returns null even when its length still matches a preset
Every returned date is built with local-calendar arithmetic; no value in this module is produced via toISOString or any UTC-anchored path
All 29 tests in dateWindow.test.ts are un-skipped and green
steps.scenario_name: dateWindow — owner-aware configuration; dateWindow — a named window ends today; dateWindow — walking the window through time; dateWindow — the window never ends in the future; dateWindow — which named window is showing
steps.implementation_notes: Replace the seven throwing bodies. Use date-fns (addDays, differenceInCalendarDays, startOfDay, isAfter) - dayjs must not enter this surface. `today` stays a parameter rather than an ambient clock read, which is what keeps the module a pure-function contract with an empty effect universe. The tests assert local Y/M/D component-wise precisely so they can fail when the suite runs outside UTC; do not satisfy them by formatting through ISO. Un-skipping is done by changing `describe.skip` to `describe` in the five blocks - leave the lazy fixture helpers as they are, because a call hoisted back to describe scope fails the file as a broken suite rather than reporting pending tests. On DEVOPS's ci-frontend-nonutc axis: no CI change is needed here and none should be added. `pnpm test` and the `pnpm run sonarreport` that CI actually invokes are already `cross-env TZ=Europe/Zurich vitest run` (Lighthouse.Frontend/package.json:12-13), so the suite has never run at UTC and environments.yaml's 'Runner clock is UTC' note under ci-frontend is wrong. Do NOT swap in the negative-offset zone environments.yaml suggests: every date in these four files is constructed at local midnight (`new Date(y, m-1, d)`, and `vi.setSystemTime` on such a value), and at a POSITIVE offset an accidental `toISOString().split('T')[0]` yields the previous calendar day and reds, while at a negative offset it yields the same day and passes. Europe/Zurich is the stronger guard for this feature; America/Los_Angeles would quietly weaken it.

steps.name: useDateRange hook - single applyDateRange write path replacing the two composable-unsafe setters
criteria: useDateRange(ownerType, defaultDateRange) seeds the window from ?startDate/?endDate when present and otherwise from defaultDateRange with the end on today; an explicit pair in the URL always wins on load
applyDateRange(start, end) performs exactly ONE setSearchParams call carrying BOTH startDate and endDate, with { replace: true }, encoded local Y/M/D - asserted on the recorded call, not inferred
handleStartDateChange and handleEndDateChange delegate to applyDateRange so there is one write path; changing one end leaves the other end's value intact in both state and the URL
An invalid date reaching either handler is ignored: no state change and no navigation
applyPreset(days) sets the window to that preset ending today, including from a window previously walked into the past
selectedPresetDays reports the matching preset while one matches, and null after either date is picked by hand
presets and stepDays are owner-aware, read from the ownerType argument
The hook's effect universe is exactly the declared one - committed window state, pending window state, one timer and one setSearchParams write; it performs no fetch and touches no browser storage
The three US-01 describe blocks in useDateRange.test.tsx are un-skipped and green: 'where the opening window comes from', 'choosing a named window', 'picking one date by hand leaves the other alone'
steps.scenario_name: useDateRange — where the opening window comes from; useDateRange — choosing a named window; useDateRange — picking one date by hand leaves the other alone
steps.implementation_notes: This is the step the whole feature rests on. The two setters being replaced each rebuild the params from the OTHER end's current-render value and from a stale searchParams, so calling them in sequence writes a window that is half old and half new and then fetches it. Build every write from the function arguments, never from closed-over state, and make applyDateRange the only place params are written. stepWindow, the pending window and canStepForward are implemented here in their non-debounced form so the returned shape is complete and honest; their describe blocks stay skipped until 02-02 adds the quiet period, and no user can reach them before 02-03 ships the control. Do not add the debounce here - it belongs with the stepper that needs it.

steps.name: DateRangePresets chip row
criteria: Renders one clickable chip per preset, in the order given, with the preset's label as its text
Clicking a chip reports that preset's days through onSelectPreset
The chip matching selectedDays carries aria-pressed="true" and every other chip carries aria-pressed="false"; when selectedDays is null no chip is pressed
The component computes no dates and reads no owner type - it renders from props and emits intent only
All 5 tests in DateRangePresets.test.tsx are un-skipped and green
steps.implementation_notes: MUI Chip in a Stack, following the visual shape of the chip row in ManualForecaster - visual precedent only, its code is not shared and dayjs must not follow it here. The selected signal is aria-pressed rather than colour or variant, so the state is available to assistive technology and assertable without reading computed style.

steps.name: Wire the chip row into DateRangeSelector and the hook into BaseMetricsView
criteria: DateRangeSelector renders the chip row above its two pickers and forwards presets, the selected days and the select handler; its two BoundedDatePicker instances, their validity guard and the absent end maxDate are unchanged
BaseMetricsView consumes useDateRange in place of its inline window state; the removed code is deleted rather than left alongside
Everything downstream of the window is untouched: the fetch effects, buildViewData, and useVisitedCategories' reset token still read the committed window exactly as before
Clicking a preset in the popover updates the header label and drives one round of metrics requests for the new window
A wiring test asserts the selector renders a chip per preset and that a click reaches the handler it was given
pnpm test green, pnpm build clean with zero warnings
steps.scenario_name: DateRangeSelector - renders the preset chip row and forwards a chip click
steps.implementation_notes: DashboardHeader is touched only to forward the preset props through to the popover; its steppers arrive in 02-04. BaseMetricsView should get smaller here - startDate, endDate, updateDateParams, handleStartDateChange and handleEndDateChange move out into the hook. Bug #5571's category-scoped fetching block in BaseMetricsView.test.tsx must stay green untouched; if it reds, the window's identity or the reset token changed and that is a regression, not a test to update. Any prop added to DateRangeSelector or DashboardHeader here must be optional, or be threaded through every existing render site: DateRangeSelectorProps is constructed explicitly at three sites in DateRangeSelector.keyboard.test.tsx (L28, L209, L297) and via a shared defaultProps in DateRangeSelector.test.tsx, and all eight DashboardHeaderProps are constructed explicitly in DashboardHeader.popover.test.tsx (L33) as well as in DashboardHeader.test.tsx. A required prop that misses one of those files fails `tsc -b`, which is this step's own zero-warning build criterion - DT-5 named this hazard as the reason DISTILL declined to widen these two prop types, and DELIVER is where it comes due.

phases.name: Walk the window through time
phases.description: Slice 02. A Delivery Lead clicks the back stepper beside the date label, the same-length window moves to the period immediately before, and every widget redraws over it - and clicking four times in a row costs one round of requests rather than four.

steps.name: REFACTOR - promote useDebouncedRevisionRun out of TeamForecastView into a shared hook
criteria: useDebouncedRevisionRun lives at src/hooks/useDebouncedRevisionRun.ts and takes its delay as a parameter defaulting to 300
TeamForecastView imports it instead of declaring it; its own DEBOUNCE_MS of 300 keeps its current value and meaning for its two existing call sites
TeamForecastView.autorun.test.tsx passes unchanged - it is the behaviour-preserving guard for this move and must not be edited to accommodate it
The move is committed separately from any feature work, as a refactor commit
steps.scenario_name: TeamForecastView autorun debounce - existing suite stays green across the move
steps.implementation_notes: Pure move plus one parameter. The effect keyed on a monotonic revision counter with clearTimeout in its cleanup is exactly the mechanism the stepper needs, and its cleanup is what makes unmount-mid-debounce safe as a property of the hook rather than something to remember. This is the one file the feature touches that it otherwise has no business in, so the existing test file is the whole safety net - run it before and after and do not modify it.

steps.name: Pending window and 500ms debounced commit in useDateRange
criteria: Each stepWindow call moves a pending window immediately and commits nothing; the committed window and the URL change only after 500ms of quiet
Four rapid clicks produce exactly ONE committed window - 28 days earlier on a team - and exactly ONE setSearchParams call
A further click inside the quiet period restarts it; nothing is committed at 499ms and the commit lands at 500ms
pendingStartDate/pendingEndDate track every click before commit while startDate/endDate still name the window the widgets are showing; isCommitPending is true across the gap and false once applied

canStepForward is false while the window ends today and true once it has been walked into the past; stepping forward from a window less than one step from today lands the end exactly on today with the length preserved
Unmounting mid-debounce commits nothing, writes no params and logs no React warning
The three remaining describe blocks in useDateRange.test.tsx are un-skipped and green: 'walking the window a period at a time', 'the window never ends in the future', 'leaving the page mid-click'
steps.scenario_name: useDateRange — walking the window a period at a time; useDateRange — the window never ends in the future; useDateRange — leaving the page mid-click
steps.implementation_notes: Use the hook promoted in 02-01 with a 500ms delay; leave its 300ms default alone for the forecast callers. The quiet period exists for a measurable reason - every committed window change resets useVisitedCategories and re-fires every fetch for the current category, so an undebounced burst is four full refetch rounds for three windows nobody asked to see. Do not weaken that reset token to absorb the burst; the burst is absorbed before the commit. The pending window must never reach the URL, so browser history gains one entry per burst rather than one per click.

steps.name: DateWindowStepper back/forward control
criteria: Renders a back and a forward icon button whose accessible names state the step size - 'Previous 7 days' and 'Next 7 days' on a team, 'Previous 28 days' and 'Next 28 days' on a portfolio
Back reports -1 and forward reports 1 through onStep
The forward button is disabled when canStepForward is false and reports nothing when clicked in that state; the back button stays enabled
The component holds no window and computes no dates - it emits a direction only
All 7 tests in DateWindowStepper.test.tsx are un-skipped and green
steps.implementation_notes: The accessible names carry the step size because below the sm breakpoint the header hides its date text and the icons become the only visible signal - the step size is stated nowhere else a narrow-screen reader can reach it.

steps.name: Wire the steppers into DashboardHeader with a not-yet-applied window treatment
criteria: DashboardHeader renders the stepper pair either side of the date label and forwards the step size, whether forward is available, and the step handler

The label renders the PENDING window so every click is visible immediately, and carries a visible not-yet-applied treatment while the pending window differs from the committed one, clearing when the commit lands
The steppers remain visible below the sm breakpoint where the date text is hidden
A header test asserts the label follows a pending window, that the treatment appears and clears, and that a stepper click reaches the handler
pnpm test green, pnpm build clean with zero warnings
steps.scenario_name: DashboardHeader - renders the window steppers and marks a window that has not been applied yet
steps.implementation_notes: The pending window is the one thing here a user could catch the product lying about - for up to half a second the label names a window the charts are not showing. The treatment has to make that state visibly provisional rather than silently wrong. Expose it through a data attribute as well as the visual treatment so the test can assert the state without pinning a colour. DashboardHeader.popover.test.tsx constructs DashboardHeaderProps explicitly and is type-checked by `tsc -b`, so a required stepper prop added here has to be threaded there too, not only into DashboardHeader.test.tsx.

steps.name: Playwright walking skeleton - a preset click and a stepper burst against a real dashboard
criteria: MetricsDateRange gains locators for the preset chips and the two steppers, and a helper that counts metrics requests across a click burst; its existing apply and applyAndWaitFor signatures are unchanged so WorkItemAgeAsOfRangeEnd.spec.ts and PredictabilityOverTime.spec.ts keep working
One spec drives the real dashboard: clicking a preset chip updates the header label and puts BOTH startDate and endDate in the URL for that window
The same spec walks the window back with repeated stepper clicks inside the quiet period and asserts ONE round of metrics requests for the settled window
The spec is actually run locally and passes before it is committed - no unrun spec or page-object locator is committed
steps.scenario_name: Metrics time horizon - a named window in one click, and a burst of steps costing one refetch
steps.implementation_notes: Extend the existing page object rather than replacing it - two shipped specs depend on its current methods. Drive the walking skeleton from seeded demo data, one thin scenario per user-visible flow; this is a sanity check that the controls are wired end to end, not a second unit suite. The request-count assertion is the HTTP-level half of the burst invariant whose hook-level half 02-02 already pins.

validation.verdict: Validated against all four wave sections of feature-delta.md, both slice files, ADR-189 and the eight scaffold files as they actually exist on disk. The nine-step decomposition, the describe-block assignment across the two useDateRange steps, and the dependency chain are correct as written; all 66 authored tests are reachable by exactly one step. The load-bearing claim in 01-02 - that the two per-end setters close over the current render's values and cannot be composed - was verified line by line against BaseMetricsView.tsx and is accurate, with the cited range 1215-1252 still current and no drift. Three narrowly-scoped amendments: two files_to_modify lists were short of existing render sites that are type-checked against the two extended components' prop types, and 01-01 gained a note correcting DEVOPS's ci-frontend-nonutc axis, where the suite already runs at TZ=Europe/Zurich and the negative-offset zone environments.yaml proposes would weaken rather than strengthen the guard for this feature's local-midnight date construction. No step is wrong in a way that needs a human decision.

checks.detail: Counted on disk, not from the wave document. dateWindow.test.ts holds 29 tests in five describe.skip blocks (6+5+7+7+4) whose names match 01-01's scenario_name exactly. useDateRange.test.tsx holds 25 in six blocks; 01-02 claims 'where the opening window comes from' (4), 'choosing a named window' (6) and 'picking one date by hand leaves the other alone' (3) = 13, and 02-02 claims 'walking the window a period at a time' (8), 'the window never ends in the future' (3) and 'leaving the page mid-click' (1) = 12. The two sets are disjoint and exhaust the file. DateRangePresets.test.tsx holds 5 in one block, DateWindowStepper.test.tsx holds 7 in one block. 29+25+5+7 = 66, matching DISTILL's scenario list one name at a time. Every block name in the roadmap matches a real describe string. One cross-step coupling is real and already anticipated: 'brings a window that was walked into the past back to today', inside 01-02's second block, calls stepWindow and advances timers, which is exactly why 01-02's notes require stepWindow implemented in non-debounced form at that step. The test passes under both the non-debounced and the later debounced implementation, so 02-02 does not red it.

Every criterion in 01-01, 01-03, 02-02 and 02-03 maps onto one or more authored assertions; no criterion asserts behaviour no test checks, and no authored test is unmentioned. Three criteria are design constraints rather than test restatements - 01-02's declared effect universe, 01-03's 'computes no dates and reads no owner type', 02-03's 'holds no window' - and those are DESIGN's contract-shape table (pure-function / bounded-change) carried forward verbatim, which is where they belong. Two mild over-reaches were found and left alone as harmless: 01-01's criteria mention a year boundary only for presetWindow while the file also tests it for shiftWindow, and 02-03's criteria name 'Next 28 days' while the portfolio test asserts only 'Previous 28 days'. Both are covered by the closing all-tests-green criterion on those steps.

Sufficient for 01-01, 01-02, 01-03, 02-01, 02-02, 02-03 and 02-05 against DESIGN's Component Decomposition and DISTILL's Scaffolds table. Two gaps found on the wiring steps. DateRangeSelectorProps is constructed explicitly at three render sites in DateRangeSelector.keyboard.test.tsx (L28, L209, L297); all eight DashboardHeaderProps are constructed explicitly in DashboardHeader.popover.test.tsx (L33). Neither file was listed. A required new prop on either component therefore fails tsc -b, which is 01-04's and 02-04's own zero-warning build criterion. DT-5 named this exact hazard as the reason DISTILL declined to widen these two prop types during DISTILL; the debt falls due in DELIVER and the file list has to carry it. Both files added, with the reason in the step notes.

01-02 genuinely needs 01-01: applyPreset, selectedPresetDays, presets, stepDays, canStepForward and the clamp all call into dateWindow, and its tests throw without those bodies. 01-04 genuinely needs both 01-02 (the hook it consumes in BaseMetricsView) and 01-03 (the component it renders in DateRangeSelector). 02-02 genuinely needs 02-01: DDD-3 and ADR-189 make the promoted revision-keyed hook the mechanism of the 500ms commit, so reordering would mean writing a second debounce idiom and then deleting it - which is the alternative ADR-189 rejected by name. 02-01 depending on 01-04 is slice ordering rather than a technical need, and it is the right call: it keeps the refactor commit at a slice boundary, which is where this repo puts refactors. 01-03 and 02-03 depend on their predecessors only through a type import, so both could in principle run earlier; the stated order is stricter than necessary but never wrong, so it is preserved.

The roadmap says dateWindow.ts everywhere and never dateWindowPresets.ts. That is correct: the file on disk is dateWindow.ts, dateWindow.test.ts imports from './dateWindow', and DateRangePresets.tsx imports DateWindowPreset from '../../../pages/Common/MetricsView/dateWindow'. DESIGN carries both names itself - Component Decomposition says dateWindowPresets.ts while its own Contract shapes table already says dateWindow.ts - and DT-2 settled it. No step, criterion or note anywhere in the roadmap still points at the DESIGN-era name.

Verified against the current file, and the claim is accurate. BaseMetricsView.tsx:1215 destructures useSearchParams; updateDateParams at L1232-1237 rebuilds from the searchParams of the render it was created in; handleStartDateChange at L1242-1246 calls updateDateParams(date, endDate) and handleEndDateChange at L1248-1252 calls updateDateParams(startDate, date), each reading the other end from the current render's closure. Calling both within one render therefore has the second call overwrite the first call's end of the window with its stale value, and updateDateParams then writes both params to the URL, which the fetch effects and useVisitedCategories' reset token read. The line numbers cited in the roadmap and in S4, DDD-5 and ADR-189 have not drifted: 1215-1252 is exactly the block. Also confirmed nearby and relied on by DDD-8 and ADR-189: ownerType is already derived at L1254-1255, so 01-04 needs no new flag to feed the hook.

useDebouncedRevisionRun is declared at TeamForecastView.tsx:30-39, module-private, reading a module-level DEBOUNCE_MS = 300 at L28, with two call sites at L318 and L396. src/hooks/useDebouncedRevisionRun.ts does not yet exist, so 02-01's target path is genuinely new. TeamForecastView.autorun.test.tsx exists (281 lines) and drives the debounce through fake timers at ten separate advanceTimersByTime(DEBOUNCE_MS) points, so it is a real guard rather than a nominal one, and the roadmap is right that it must not be edited to accommodate the move. One thing a crafter should not be surprised by: DEBOUNCE_MS has a third use at TeamForecastView.tsx:237, in a raw useEffect that does not go through the hook, so the constant stays declared in that file after the move. The criterion already says its DEBOUNCE_MS keeps its current value, and a mistake here fails the build immediately, so no amendment was made.

No step lists useCategorySelection.ts, widgetFetchRequirements or getFetchKeysForCategories in files_to_modify, and no criterion would be satisfied by changing the reset token. The constraint is stated positively three times rather than only in the out_of_scope list: 01-04 requires that useVisitedCategories' reset token still reads the committed window exactly as before and that Bug #5571's category-scoped block in BaseMetricsView.test.tsx stays green untouched, and 02-02 states that the burst is absorbed before the commit and that the token must not be weakened to absorb it. That matches DDD-9, the Reuse Analysis DO NOT TOUCH row, ADR-189's rejected alternative and the coexistence matrix entry.

01-01 forbids toISOString and any UTC-anchored path by name and requires local-calendar arithmetic; 01-02 requires the single write to carry both params encoded local Y/M/D, asserted on the recorded call. No criterion or note anywhere would be satisfied by an ISO path. The scaffolded tests back this: dateWindow.test.ts compares [year, month, day] component-wise and useDateRange.test.tsx formats through a local asLocalIso helper, never through toISOString. Amended 01-01's notes with what the runner actually does, because the upstream statement of this axis is wrong in a way that could cause someone to make the guard weaker in good faith - see the ci-frontend-nonutc amendment.

amendments.change: Added a paragraph on DEVOPS's ci-frontend-nonutc axis: no CI change is needed, and the negative-offset zone environments.yaml proposes must not be adopted. pnpm test and the pnpm run sonarreport that CI actually invokes are already cross-env TZ=Europe/Zurich vitest run (Lighthouse.Frontend/package.json:12-13).
amendments.why: DEVOPS's Environment Matrix declares ci-frontend-nonutc non-ceremonial and its CI/CD Pipeline Outline calls for the date suites to run a second time at a negative-offset zone, while environments.yaml notes under ci-frontend that the runner clock is UTC. Both are wrong on the facts. TZ appears nowhere in .github/workflows because it is pinned in the package.json script instead, so the suite has never run at UTC. And the proposed direction is inverted for this feature: every date in the four scaffold files is built at local midnight, where a positive offset makes toISOString().split('T')[0] yield the previous calendar day and red, while a negative offset yields the same day and passes. Adopting America/Los_Angeles would replace a working guard with one blind to exactly the Bug #5566 slip it exists to catch. Recorded in the step rather than acted on, so the plan does not silently skip a declared non-ceremonial axis.

amendments.change: Added Lighthouse.Frontend/src/components/Common/DateRangeSelector/DateRangeSelector.keyboard.test.tsx and Lighthouse.Frontend/src/pages/Common/MetricsView/DashboardHeader.popover.test.tsx, with the reason appended to implementation_notes.
amendments.why: DT-5: 'in TypeScript a skipped test is still type-checked', which is why DISTILL declined to widen DateRangeSelector's and DashboardHeader's prop types and deferred the integration assertions to DELIVER. This is the step where that widening happens. DateRangeSelectorProps is constructed explicitly at three sites in DateRangeSelector.keyboard.test.tsx and DashboardHeaderProps at one site in DashboardHeader.popover.test.tsx; a required new prop that misses either file fails tsc -b and so fails this step's own criterion of a clean zero-warning pnpm build.

amendments.change: Added Lighthouse.Frontend/src/pages/Common/MetricsView/DashboardHeader.popover.test.tsx, with the reason appended to implementation_notes.
amendments.why: Same DT-5 mechanism. This step adds the stepper props to DashboardHeaderProps; DashboardHeader.popover.test.tsx constructs all eight existing props explicitly at L33 and is compiled by tsc -b, so it has to be threaded there and not only into DashboardHeader.test.tsx.

notes_for_the_orchestrator: Slice 01 ships with no Playwright coverage. slice-01-named-windows-in-one-click.md lists a walking-skeleton spec in its IN scope, but DT-8 and DISTILL's Handoff to DELIVER place the single E2E at the end of slice 02, and the roadmap follows DISTILL. Nothing is lost - 02-05's criteria include the preset-chip click, the header label and both URL params, which is the E2E remainder the AT completeness audit assigns to AC-01.4 - but the preset control's end-to-end wiring is unverified for the whole of slice 01's review. Left unamended because the later wave governs and one combined spec matches this repo's E2E minimalism; flagged because the user reviews slices individually.

KPI-6 - that no existing Team or Portfolio opens on a different window than before - is the one KPI verified by hand, before/after on the dev instance restored from a production backup. No step owns it and out_of_scope does not name it. It is a finalization concern rather than a crafter concern, and it sits inside 'the user reviews the delivered slices first', but it should be answered explicitly rather than allowed to lapse.
The Final Wave Review Gate that DISTILL recorded as DELIVER's entry condition is cleared by commit a18ebdd6a.
